cases.original_question: Which are the top 10 areas rich in both sections and tables? (high implementation difficulty)
cases.original_query: MATCH (sec:Section)-[:CONTAINS_TABLE]->(tbl:TSTable) WITH sec, count(tbl) AS tableCount WHERE tableCount >= 3 MATCH (sec)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(sp:Spec) OPTIONAL MATCH (sec)-[:HAS_SUB_SECTION]->(sub:Section) RETURN sp.specNumber, sec.sectionNumber, sec.sectionTitle, tableCount, count(sub) AS subSectionCount ORDER BY tableCount DESC LIMIT 10
cases.fixed_by_original_wording: Top 10 areas rich in both sections and tables; 10 is explicit, the two-axis richness metric is not.
cases.exact_missing_criterion: How section richness and table richness jointly determine the ranking; area identity and recursive extent remain separate.
cases.original_query_and_legacy_contract_count: The preserved query explicitly applies tableCount >= 3 and orders by tableCount alone; its old contract records cardinality 10 and tableCount DESC.
